narrative:
The model estimates that you have about a 45 percent chance of not completing your final year successfully. That is not a certainty, but it is a high enough risk that your school requires you to take remedial courses as a safety net. The goal is not to punish you, but to give you extra support before problems become harder to reverse.

When the model looked at your situation, the most powerful signal was that you said you do not want to continue into higher education. Among students who passed, every single one reported wanting to pursue higher education. Your answer is the main reason the model leaned toward failure, not because wanting higher education is the only good path, but because it often reflects how connected a student feels to their schoolwork. If you see little point in the final year, motivation can drop and grades can suffer.

The second factor actually worked in your favor. You have never failed a class before, and that history of past success is a strong positive sign. It shows you have the ability and prior knowledge to do well.

The third factor also pointed toward passing. You said your weekend alcohol consumption is very low. Healthy habits often support steady academic effort, and this pattern is consistent with students who succeed.

So your risk mainly comes from a lack of interest in higher education, not from poor ability or bad habits. You should talk with a counselor or family member about what you want after school. Even if university is not your goal, exploring career paths and seeing how your current subjects connect to those paths can make this year feel more meaningful and worth your effort.
